name: District of Columbia
one: District of Columbia mails a ballot to every registered voter. Below: how to send it back and the deadlines.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in District of Columbia, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Getting your ballot

Monday, October 19Passed

A request to have your ballot sent somewhere other than your D.C. home had to reach the Board by Monday, October 19, 2026 (the rule: no later than the 15th day before the election). This deadline has passed. Military and overseas voters may still ask until Saturday, October 31, 2026. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

By mail: postmarked on or before Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and received by the Board by Friday, November 13, 2026. In a drop box, at a Vote Center or at the Board's office: by 8:00 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. (official page)

That date has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Sunday, November 1, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on District of Columbia’s own site

At school away from home, in District of Columbia or in another state? What District of Columbia says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. The Board of Elections mails a ballot to every active registered voter at their D.C. address. You only need to ask for a ballot if you will be away from your D.C. home during the election and want it sent somewhere else. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Only voters who will be away from their D.C. home need to ask. Use the Board's online Mail Ballot Request Form to have your ballot sent to the address where you will be. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Use the postage-paid return envelope that comes with your ballot. It must be postmarked on or before Election Day and arrive by Friday, November 13, 2026. (official page)
  • Drop box. Any of the Board's 55 mail ballot drop boxes, at any time from Friday, October 9 at 11:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. (official page)
  • In person. Hand it in at any Vote Center or at the Board of Elections office, 1015 Half Street SE, Suite 750, by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

What the envelope needs

You must sign and date the Voter's Oath on the back of the return envelope, or your vote will not count. No witness is needed. If you registered by mail or online and this is your first time voting in D.C., put a copy of an ID inside the return envelope: a current government photo ID, or a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck or other government document with your name and address, dated no more than 90 days before the election. Without it, your ballot is set aside and counted only if you send the Board a copy. If there is a problem with your signature, the Board will contact you. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on District of Columbia’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 26, 2026 to Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Early Vote Centers are open every day from Monday, October 26 through Sunday, November 1, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. You can also register at an Early Vote Center and vote the same day. On Election Day, Vote Centers are open 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. (official page)

Students

At school in District of Columbia, away from home

D.C. is one city with one election office, so there is no 'elsewhere in the state.' For students living at a D.C. college: the Board says a student may register and vote in D.C. after living at their campus address for 30 days before the election, and should list the residence hall on the registration form. A college housing statement or a lease counts as proof of address. The Board also says to check with your financial aid office first that D.C. residency and registering here will not affect your aid. The Board also says a student from another state attending college in D.C. may vote absentee in their home state instead. (official page)

At school in another state, with District of Columbia as home

The Board says a D.C. resident going to college in another state can still vote as a D.C. resident by asking for an absentee ballot. The request had to reach the Board no later than the 15th day before the election, which for this election was Monday, October 19, 2026. (official page)

Military and overseas

Service members, their families and U.S. citizens living abroad can register and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA), or with any signed written request, sent by mail, in person, by e-mail or by fax ((202) 347-2648). The ballot can be sent to you by mail, e-mail or fax. Requests should reach the Board no later than Saturday, October 31, 2026 (3 days before the election). If you use the FPCA to register as well, it had to be received by Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (21 days before the election); that date has passed. A ballot returned by e-mail or fax must arrive by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day; a mailed one must be sent by Election Day and arrive within 10 days after. If your ballot may not come in time, you can use the Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot from FVAP. (official page)

District of Columbia in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The Board's calendar says it is subject to change and marks the drop box dates as tentative; check the Board's site close to Election Day.
  • The Board's calendar gives Thursday, November 19, 2026 as the last day to fix (cure) a problem with a mail ballot.
  • Mail ballots went out to every active registered voter starting about September 28, 2026 (tentative date on the Board's calendar). If you make a mistake on your ballot or lose any of it, the Board asks you to call 1-866-DC-VOTES (1-866-328-6837) right away; if you are worried about getting or returning your ballot in time, it asks you to call (202) 727-2525.
  • Not yet registered? D.C. lets you register and vote the same day at an Early Vote Center (October 26 to November 1) or at a Vote Center on Election Day.
